tweets.text:
Come on, man. Your entire response revolves around an unconfirmed and probably false estimate from SemiAnalysis. GPT-4’s parameter count was never disclosed. The number you give is simply SemiAnalysis’s headline eye catching estimate based on unnamed sources

Even under that estimate, 220B only counts the activated experts. SemiAnalysis estimated 280B active per forward pass once shared attention is included

The figures for Fable, Spud and Astra are also unconfirmed. You are using rumors as historical data

The numbers we can confirm show continued scaling. Qwen3.8-Max has 2.4T parameters and Kimi K3 has 2.8T. Optimisation and parameter scaling are still happening simultaneously

The 100T versus 25T comparison is also entirely hypothetical. You assume recurrence reduces the parameters needed for equal capability by 4x, then use that assumption to conclude future models will need 4x fewer parameters. That is circular logic based on nothing 

Even if it did, looping a 25T model four times still requires four sequential passes and repeated HBM reads. It reduces unique weight storage, but not HBM bandwidth or accelerator demand by the same amount

So yes, recurrence can reduce HBM required per unit of capability. It does not follow that total HBM demand falls when parameters, inference volume, context, agents and test-time compute are all increasing

There has never been a trend toward fewer parameters. The trend has always been toward optimization + more parameters

That’s Jevons’ paradox at the model level

Even if we achieve ASI with an optimized number of parameters, why would parameter scaling suddenly stop?

Even the researchers behind the cited study found that their recurrent model was better at reasoning but weaker at memorizing facts. They expect future systems to combine recurrence with MoE

And even if parameter counts don’t keep scaling, which I doubt, intelligence would become cheaper, increasing its demand and, ultimately, HBM demand

Anyway, I really don’t see a world where models stop scaling

Samsung (005930.KS) challenges $TSM production with Panel-Level-Packaging

Samsung plans to bring its 415×510mm FOPLP platform into mass production around 2028, sticking with a significantly larger panel format than TSMC’s 310×310mm standard

The larger Samsung panel offers 2.2× the usable area of a 310×310mm panel, potentially providing meaningful unit-cost advantages. Samsung also already has high-volume PLP manufacturing experience from mobile and wearable chips, giving it existing infrastructure and expertise in warpage control

The challenge is moving the technology into AI server packaging, where integrating logic dies and HBM is considerably more difficult. TSMC also has an established advantage because its 310×310mm format has already attracted a large equipment, materials and OSAT ecosystem

Samsung is also targeting glass-substrate mass production in 2029–2030 as package sizes increase and conventional ABF substrates face growing technical and supply constraints

Perhaps most interestingly, Samsung is aggressively using AI in packaging R&D. Physics-Informed Neural Networks are being applied to signal integrity, power integrity and thermal simulations, reportedly reducing some engineering workflows from one year to a single day

DIGITIMES: Memory boom stays strong into 2027

DIGITIMES argues the memory upcycle is accelerating as AI infrastructure drives demand for DRAM, NAND and HBM, with supply remaining tight until meaningful new capacity starts arriving in 2027–2028

The biggest structural change is that memory demand is increasingly tied to AI accelerator architectures rather than PCs and smartphones. HBM4 adoption accelerates through 2026–27, followed by HBM4E, while Nvidia’s Vera platform moves toward removable SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X modules

Enterprise storage is also benefiting. PCIe Gen6 enterprise SSDs are entering production, with Samsung and Micron already ramping products and Phison and Silicon Motion expected to launch Gen6 controllers in 2027

Capacity additions are substantial but mostly back-end loaded:

· Samsung: Pyeongtaek P5 production in 2028, Yongin DRAM in 2029, new Onyang HBM packaging in 2029.

· $SKHY: M15X already ramping in 2026, Yongin DRAM from Q1 2027, P&T7 HBM packaging by end-2027, Indiana HBM packaging in H2 2028.

· $MU: Tungluo expansion, Hiroshima DRAM, Singapore HBM packaging from 2027, new NAND capacity in H2 2028, Idaho expansion in 2027–28 and New York DRAM from 2030.
